content.value_statement: Unclear commit messages make project history difficult to review and maintain. This skill analyzes staged changes and guides you to concise Conventional Commit messages.
actual_capabilities: Reviews staged changes with git diff --staged guidance.
Suggests Conventional Commit types, scopes, summaries, bodies, and footers.
Explains how to document breaking changes in commit messages.
Provides examples for feature, fix, refactor, infrastructure, and multi-file commits.
Guides selective staging and amendment workflows with standard Git commands.
limitations: It relies on the available staged diff and cannot infer unstaged changes.
It suggests commit text but does not verify project-specific commit policies.
It does not run tests, stage files, create commits, or modify repository history.
Generated messages require human review for accuracy and sensitive information.

use_cases.title: Prepare a feature commit
use_cases.description: Review a staged feature diff and create a focused Conventional Commit message.

use_cases.title: Improve pull request history
use_cases.description: Standardize commit messages before opening a pull request for easier review.

use_cases.title: Document a breaking API change
use_cases.description: Write a commit subject and footer that clearly communicate an incompatible change.

prompt_templates.title: Suggest a basic commit message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and suggest one concise Conventional Commit message.

prompt_templates.title: Choose type and scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my staged diff. Recommend the best commit type and scope, then write a subject under 50 characters.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a multi-file change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes across several files. Create a Conventional Commit subject and a short body explaining why the related changes belong together.

prompt_templates.title: Describe a breaking change
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my staged API changes. Draft a Conventional Commit message with a clear BREAKING CHANGE footer and migration guidance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Maintainer releasing an incompatible API change

output_examples.input: Staged changes add email validation to the registration form.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: fix(form): validate registration email

output_examples.input: Staged changes move authentication logic into a service and update tests.
output: Suggested message: refactor(auth): extract authentication service

output_examples.input: Staged changes replace the API response structure.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: feat(api)!: revise response structure. Include a footer that identifies the breaking change and migration need.

best_practices: Review the staged diff before accepting a suggested message.
Use one logical change per commit whenever possible.
Remove secrets, personal data, and unrelated details from commit messages.
anti_patterns: Do not use a generic message such as update or fix stuff.
Do not combine unrelated features and fixes in one commit message.
Do not mark a change as breaking unless users must change their code or configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Git commit?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and suggested commit messages only.

faq.question: What commit format does it use?
faq.answer: It recommends the Conventional Commits format with type, optional scope, description, body, and footer.

faq.question: Can it review multiple staged files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help summarize related staged changes into one focused message.

faq.question: Can it help with breaking changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to use an exclamation mark or BREAKING CHANGE footer.

faq.question: Does it run tests or modify files?
faq.answer: No. It does not run tests, change files, stage content, or alter Git history.

faq.question: Should I use every suggested message unchanged?
faq.answer: No. Review each suggestion and adjust it to reflect the actual change and your project rules.
